World.title: Vice President Mutale Nalumango meets Chifunabuli chiefs
World.content:
Vice President Mutale Nalumango says government recognises traditional leaders as key partners in governance and development.

‎During her working visit in Chifunabuli District of Luapula Province, Mrs Nalumango met traditional leaders of the Abena Ng’umbo, including Chief Chitembo, Chief Mbulu, Chief Mulongwe, and representatives of Senior Chief Mwewa and Chief Mwansakombe.

She highlighted various developmental programmes that the government is undertaking across the country to improve people’s livelihoods, including the free education policy.

‎

‎”Your royal highnesses, the free education policy here in Chifunabuli District has since its introduction for instance brought 400 pupils back to school,” she said.

Ms Nalumango therefore stated that continuity of the developmental projects hinges on the electorate turning out to re-elect the United Party for National Development (UPND) on 13th August.

She added that the UPND had responded to calls for the construction of the Musaila – Lubwe – Kasaba Road to bituminous standard, a project which has commenced, with contractors already on site.

‎And Chief Chitembo hailed the government for the free education policy, and the roadworks which are now ongoing.

‎

‎The Vice President also met the Pastors Fellowship, commending their fish farming project which is aimed at creating opportunities for youths.

‎

Chifunabuli Pastors Fellowship Chairperson, Dominic Mubanga, said the clergy would remain steadfast in their prayer for government as they continue to administer the necessary critical development across the country.

‎

Reverend Mubanga said the clergy are cognisant of the various government initiatives such as the free education policy, enhanced Constituency Development Fund (CDF), including the current roadworks on the Musaila-Lubwe- Kasaba Road.

‎

‎He said the Chifunabuli Pastor’s Fellowship stands ready in responding to the call as partners in development.

‎

‎Addressing civil servants, Mrs Nalumango urged them to work as a unified unit with the government to ensure effective delivery of development.

‎

‎She reminded them that public servants must be in sync with the government’s policy to guarantee smooth implementation of programmes.

‎

‎The Vice President encouraged civil servants to also take up farming to ensure personal food security and boost their income, tendencies aligning with national production targets.

‎

‎She cited the government’s goal to increase maize output to 10 million tonnes and soya beans to three million tonnes among other policy targets in different sectors of the economy.

‎

‎Chifunabuli District Education Standards Officer, Grace Kambobe, reported that since the commencement of free education policy, learner enrolment has surged from 26,522 in 2021 to 41,732 currently.

‎She added that 403 teachers have since been recruited in Chifunabuli and many schools in the district are benefiting from the school feeding programme.

‎

‎Ms Kambobe also highlighted the Keeping Girls in School (KGS) initiative as a key factor in boosting retention rates in the district.

‎

‎Meanwhile, Lubwe Secondary Boarding School Headteacher, Misheck Chirwa, expressed gratitude on behalf of civil servants to Mrs Nalumango for her visit to the area.

He also thanked the government through the Vice President for a fully-fledged boarding secondary school in Mwewa chiefdom.

World.title: He was Dinning with the Enemy – HH Goes for Nkombo
World.content:
Hichilema tears into Nkombo, exposes two decades of “betrayal” in blistering Mazabuka address

MAZABUKA, July 24, 2026 — President Hakainde Hichilema unloaded years of pent-up frustration on his former ally Gary Nkombo before a packed Mazabuka crowd, opening with a question that set the tone for everything that followed. “Can I spill the beans?” he asked, and then did precisely that, for the better part of his address.

He took the crowd back to the darkest days of opposition politics, when the Patriotic Front (PF) was, in his telling, actively hunting him down. He named Kaizer Zulu, the political operative he says wanted him dead, and said that within a month of that threat, Nkombo was already dining and drinking with the very man. “A month later, you would find Nkombo in Kafue enjoying himself, dining with a person who wanted to kill me,” he said, his disbelief evident. “What can one person think of Nkombo?”

He said the pattern repeated itself even closer to home, with the very officials who had persecuted him. While Stephen Kampyongo was serving as Minister of Home Affairs and had him teargassed during the day, Nkombo would be found drinking and dining with the same people that night, without a shred of shame. It did not stop there either. The President recalled that when Bowman Lusambo was still fighting the UPND on behalf of PF, Nkombo was later spotted sharing a beer with him too, as if the years of struggle counted for nothing.

Hichilema said he confronted Nkombo directly about this pattern of behaviour, and each time the response was the same, a shrug and a soft apology. “I have heard, Mr President,” Nkombo would say, before doing it all again. “He is a rebel,” Hichilema declared. “He started being rebellious a long time ago. One person who does not change.” He said only restraint had kept him from reacting more forcefully over the years. “God gave me a chest for cooling my heart, my temper, not for being upset with people or fighting people,” he told the crowd, a line that drew loud approval even as his own irritation was plain to see.

The President then turned to the present, accusing Nkombo of quietly throwing his weight behind Tonse-Pamodzi Alliance candidate Brian Mundubile. He pointed to the symbols on their respective ballots, Nkombo’s candle and Mundubile’s lamp, and told the crowd the resemblance was no accident. “The lamp and the candle are one thing, and that is how they planned it,” he said, before putting a direct question to his supporters: would they follow Mundubile through Gary Nkombo? The crowd roared back that they would not. “Thank you,” Hichilema said. “Don’t follow that friend of mine in the name of Gary Nkombo, for 20 years.”

What seemed to sting the President most was the ingratitude. Nkombo, he said, owed his entire political career to him, yet had never once offered a word of thanks. “Gary could have come to say thank you for allowing me to be in parliament,” he said, adding that on top of everything else, Nkombo had refused to vote in support of Bill 7 when the party needed him most.

He then walked the crowd through what he described as a final, private attempt to resolve things man to man. He said he had summoned Nkombo, not to State House, but to his own home, and sat him down in the presence of a witness. “I am a person with a big chest, simply a man with a big heart,” he said. There, he asked Nkombo not to contest the Mazabuka seat, telling him plainly that he had wronged the UPND. Once the party’s adoption process had run its course, Hichilema said he went further still and asked Nkombo to campaign for him instead, an olive branch he insisted others in Nkombo’s position had gracefully accepted.

To prove the point, he ran through the list himself. Former Minister of Education Douglas Siakalima had been asked not to stand and had not stood, and was out on the trail campaigning for the party. Sikumba, present at the rally itself, had also been asked to step aside and was doing the same, campaigning loyally rather than sulking. And former Minister of Foreign Affairs Mulambo Haimbe, also present, had accepted the same request without complaint and was campaigning too.

“All the mentioned are campaigning,” Hichilema said, driving the final nail in. “Who is Nkombo not to respect UPND, and be like the others?”

World.title: VP Nalumango outlines UPND campaign promises to Chifunabuli
World.content:
Vice President Mutale Nalumango has laid out a series of campaign promises to the people of Chifunabuli District, urging them to re-elect the United Party for National Development (UPND) on 13th August to ensure these commitments are fulfilled.

Mrs Nalumango promised that the free education policy would continue, citing its impact so far in the district.

“Your royal highnesses, the free education policy here in Chifunabuli District has since its introduction for instance brought 400 pupils back to school,” she said.

She further backed this promise with data from Chifunabuli District Education Standards Officer, Grace Kambobe, who reported that learner enrolment has surged from 26,522 in 2021 to 41,732 currently, with 403 teachers recruited and many schools benefiting from the school feeding programme and the Keeping Girls in School initiative.

The Vice President promised that the construction of the Musaila – Lubwe – Kasaba Road to bituminous standard is already underway, with contractors on site — a project she said the UPND had responded to after calls from the community.

Mrs Nalumango promised the continuation of various developmental programmes across the country, including the enhanced Constituency Development Fund (CDF), as acknowledged by the Chifunabuli Pastors Fellowship.

Addressing civil servants, she promised that effective delivery of development would be achieved if public servants work as a unified unit with the government and remain in sync with government policy to guarantee smooth implementation of programmes.

The Vice President also promised to push for national production targets, encouraging civil servants to take up farming to boost food security and income, citing the government’s goal to increase maize output to 10 million tonnes and soya beans to three million tonnes.

She further promised continued support for education infrastructure, with Lubwe Secondary Boarding School Headteacher, Misheck Chirwa, thanking the government through the Vice President for a fully-fledged boarding secondary school already delivered in Mwewa chiefdom.

Mrs Nalumango stated that continuity of all these developmental projects hinges on the electorate turning out to re-elect the UPND on 13th August.

Traditional leaders, including Chief Chitembo, have already hailed the government for the free education policy and the roadworks, while the Pastors Fellowship, through Chairperson Dominic Mubanga, said the clergy stands ready as partners in development and would remain steadfast in prayer for government as they continue to administer critical development across the country.

World.title: Solwezi woman dies due to phone battery explosion
World.content:
A 23- year- old woman of Ikelenge District of North-Western Province has died after she was struck on the neck by a cellphone battery that exploded as a result of the fire.

North-Western Province Commissioner of Police, Brighton Mwale, confirmed the incident in a statement issued in Solwezi yesterday and identified the victim as Jean Ntambu aged 22 of Matoka village.

He said the matter was reported on July 22, 2026 by the victim’s brother, Guard Ntambu, aged 26, that his young sister, Jean Ntambu, aged 23, of the same abode, died after she was struck by a cell phone battery that exploded on the fire and caused her to sustain a deep cut on her neck at about 18:00 hours at Matoka village.

Mr Siwale said brief facts of the matter are that on 22nd July, 2026 at about 17:00 hours the deceased was cleaning the surrounding and hipped the dirty at one point and set it on fire.

He explained that while burning the dirt, the deceased sat near the fire without realising that amongst the dirt was a dead cell phone battery which exploded and some particles hit her on her neck causing her to sustain a deep cut and heavy bleeding.

Mr Siwale said the victim was rushed to a rural health post where she was attended to and later transferred to Kalene Mission Hospital where she was pronounced dead upon arrival.

“Acting on the report police rushed to Ikelenge Rural Health Post where the victim was rushed to and found the health personnel attending to the victim, and the condition was critical. A deep cut on the neck and severe bleeding was observed,” Mr Siwale said.

He said the body of the deceased has since been deposited in Kalene Mission Hospital mortuary awaiting postmortem examination and burial.

Mr Siwale has warned members of the public to be mindful in the manner and way they dispose of gadgets waste to avoid similar unfortunate circumstances in their communities in the future.

World.title: 8 Not 7: ECZ’s Unopposed Seat Count Falls Short, and Lumezi North Goes Unexplained
World.content:
Eight, Not Seven: ECZ’s Unopposed Seat Count Falls Short, and Lumezi North Goes Unexplained

Lusaka. A review of the Electoral Commission of Zambia’s (ECZ) own nomination records has turned up two discrepancies ahead of the 13 August general election. One is an undercount in the number of uncontested National Assembly seats. The other is the unexplained disappearance of an entire constituency from the Commission’s official candidate list.

In a public announcement this month, ECZ told stakeholders that, apart from the presidential race, several candidates had been declared unopposed across the mayoral, National Assembly, and local government by-elections. The Commission recorded six unopposed mayoral candidates out of 116 districts, seven unopposed National Assembly candidates out of 226 constituencies, and 176 unopposed candidates for local government out of 1,858 wards.

A check of ECZ’s own Notice of Validly Nominated Candidates for the 2026 Parliamentary Elections, dated 22 July 2026, tells a different story. Eight constituencies carry only one validly nominated candidate each, not seven. All eight went to the United Party for National Development (UPND): Keembe West in Central Province, Zambezi West and Liuwa in the west, and five constituencies clustered in Southern Province, namely Choma South, Dundumwezi, Kalomo South, Kazungula North, and Sinazongwe.

The gap is one seat. But it sits inside a document that candidates, party agents, and voters are meant to treat as authoritative. ECZ has not publicly clarified which figure is correct.

A separate and more serious gap concerns Lumezi North constituency in Eastern Province’s Lumezi District. The constituency does not appear anywhere in the 22 July nomination notice. It is missing from the contested seats, missing from the unopposed seats, and missing without a single explanatory note.

The reason traces back to a death. Three candidates had lodged nominations for Lumezi North in May: Anderson Banda of the ruling UPND, Nebby Manda of the Leadership Movement, and Clement Mwale, standing for the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) under the Tonse Pamodzi Alliance banner. Mwale had served as Lumezi Council Chairperson between 2016 and 2021. He died in the early hours of 16 July 2026. Tonse Pamodzi Alliance’s Eastern Province chairperson, Maxson Nkhoma, confirmed the death in a statement.

Zambian election law changed significantly in 2025. Under Constitutional Amendment No. 13 of that year, a candidate who resigns or is disqualified by a court after nominations close no longer forces the Commission to cancel that election. The reform was designed to stop late withdrawals from disrupting the vote. Death, however, was kept as a distinct exception. Article 52(6)(c) of the Constitution still requires ECZ to cancel the poll for that constituency and give the candidate’s sponsoring party thirty days to nominate a replacement. ECZ’s own nomination guidance sets out the same rule. ECZ Commissioner McDonald Chipenzi, briefing reporters in Dubai on ballot paper printing, confirmed that this obligation applies to Lumezi North following Mwale’s death.

The legal process is not in question. What is missing is any acknowledgement of it in the document meant to inform the public. Anyone working from the 22 July notice alone, a resident of Lumezi North, a journalist, a party agent, would have no way of knowing why their constituency is not there. It could just as easily read as a printing fault, a missed submission, or an unresolved dispute. The notice does not say otherwise.

Neither issue is, on its own, a major scandal. An undercount of one seat is an administrative slip. A constituency’s absence, once explained, turns out to rest on a lawful and defensible basis. That is precisely the point. These are small, answerable questions, and ECZ has not answered them.

Zambian elections run across 226 constituencies, 116 districts, and 1,858 wards, at enormous cost and under real time pressure. Nobody disputes that ECZ is stretched thin. But a national election depends on public confidence in the paperwork as much as in the polling itself. That confidence is built one clarified query at a time. It is not damaged by any single unanswered question so much as by a habit of treating small questions from the public as beneath a response. A one-line note explaining Lumezi North, or a corrected figure in the unopposed count, would have cost the Commission almost nothing and closed both matters before they became a story.

ECZ should treat no query as too small, no discrepancy as too minor, and no member of the public raising one as a nuisance. That habit of responsiveness, more than any single correction, is what keeps an electoral process credible in the eyes of the people it serves.

This publication has sought clarification from ECZ on both the correct number of uncontested National Assembly seats and the current status of the Lumezi North re-nomination process. This story will be updated with the Commission’s response.

source: ECZ’s Notice of Validly Nominated Candidates for the 2026 Parliamentary Elections (22 July 2026), ECZ’s public announcement on unopposed candidates, ECZ’s published nominations guidance, Constitutional Amendment No. 13 of 2025,

World.title: South Africa: Gauteng Taxi Strike Averted After Talks - South African News Briefs - July 24, 2026
World.content:
Gauteng Taxi Strike Averted After Talks

A planned Gauteng taxi shutdown has been called off after crisis talks between the provincial government and taxi industry leaders, reports EWN. The Gauteng Department of Transport, SANTACO and the National Taxi Alliance agreed to continue negotiations over issues including operating licences. Another meeting has been scheduled within 14 days. Taxi operators apologised for the uncertainty and said they had chosen dialogue over disruption. They assured commuters that services would continue uninterrupted.

Court to Rule on Ramaphosa Impeachment Bid



The Western Cape High Court is set to rule on President Cyril Ramaphosa's urgent application to suspend Parliament's Section 89 Impeachment Committee temporarily, reports SABC News. Ramaphosa seeks to review the independent panel's Phala Phala report. The committee was established after the Constitutional Court ordered impeachment proceedings to continue. Political analyst Professor Zwelinzima Ndevu said the judgment would clarify both the President's legal rights and the committee's mandate.

State Witness Continues Testimony in Mapisa-Nqakula Trial

The Pretoria High Court has heard that the State's key witness in the corruption trial of former National Assembly Speaker Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula said she was still expected to pay a bribe after being robbed, reports EWN. SANDF contractor Nombasa Ntsondwa-Ndlovu testified that although robbers stole R12,000 from her in 2017, she managed to protect R200,000 allegedly intended for Mapisa-Nqakula. The State alleges the former Speaker solicited R4.5 million in bribes between 2016 and 2019, receiving R2.1 million. Mapisa-Nqakula faces 12 corruption charges.

World.title: Sudan: 80 Sudanese Leave Uganda On Voluntary Return Flight
World.content:
Amsterdam / Kampala — The 11th voluntary return flight carrying Sudanese refugees from Uganda to Sudan departed on Thursday with 80 returnees on board. The flight travelled to Port Sudan Airport aboard a Tarco Aviation aircraft and was sponsored by Sudan's General Intelligence Service.

The Higher Committee for the Voluntary Repatriation of Sudanese Refugees from Uganda said the flight forms part of the ongoing voluntary return programme for Sudanese wishing to return home, in coordination with the relevant authorities.

The committee said it had completed the procedures before departure, including issuing the returnees with their airline tickets and the travel documents required for the journey to Sudan.

It added that the flight is part of continuing efforts to organise regular voluntary return flights and facilitate the return of Sudanese who wish to go back to their country.

The flight is the 11th under the voluntary return programme launched from Uganda earlier this year. Several flights have already been operated to Port Sudan, while registration of those wishing to return and coordination with the relevant authorities continues.

World.title: Sudan: 'U.S. Congress Should Pass New Bills On Sudan' - Human Rights Watch
World.content:
Washington — The US Congress is currently considering two bills on Sudan: the Preventing External Aggression and Conflict Escalation (PEACE) in Sudan Act of 2026 in the Senate and US Engagement in Sudanese Peace Act in the House of Representatives. Human Rights Watch (HRW) asserts that "by pushing for such legislation, Congress can play a vital role in responding to the human rights crisis in Sudan."

A statement this week, penned by Nicholas Freund of the Human Rights Watch (HRW) Washington agency, points out how "these bills contain several positive initiatives but should go further on accountability," and emphasises how the organisation has documented widespread abuses by both the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), including attacks against civilians by both groups, widespread sexual violence by the RSF, and evidence of ethnic cleansing by the RSF in West Darfur.

"Although the administration has taken important steps on Sudan, including sanctions on both parties to the conflict, the US government has failed, along with the international community, to apply sufficient pressure to stop the atrocities and improve humanitarian conditions. Both bills bolster the US government's response to the conflict, including by reinforcing the role of the special envoy on Sudan, which is currently vacant, and enabling the US to sanction those responsible for abuses in the country," the HRW statement says.



It underscores that HRW has consistently urged the UN Security Council to authorise the deployment of a civilian protection mission in Sudan, pointing out that the House's legislation authorises US government support for a United Nations, African Union, or multinational force in Sudan.

"Both bills would also require the US government to identify foreign governments' activities in Sudan and whether they are in violation of the UN arms embargo. The House bill would ban the sale of major defence equipment to any government supplying weapons to the RSF or SAF, unless waived for national security reasons," HRW says.

"These are welcome proposals given the growing evidence that the RSF has received military support from the UAE and recent Human Rights Watch findings that a UAE-based company hired Colombian private military contractors that trained at UAE military bases before deploying to Sudan to support the RSF.

"Congress should enhance accountability measures in the bills to ensure the US government plays an active role in seeking a comprehensive approach to accountability in Sudan. Congress should direct the administration to support ongoing investigation efforts of serious international crimes, including support to the collection and preservation of evidence for future accountability processes to advance justice for victims.

Close 

"By pushing for such legislation, Congress can play a vital role in responding to the human rights crisis in Sudan," HRW concludes.

(Source: HRW)

World.title: Zimbabwe: Hybrid Seed Leading Revival of Cotton Farming in Zimbabwe
World.content:
A new generation of hybrid cotton seeds is giving Zimbabwean farmers fresh reason for optimism. Developed to deliver higher yields and withstand climate shocks and pests, the seeds are helping to boost productivity and improve livelihoods in farming communities.

For more than two decades, 56-year-old cotton farmer Aleck Bikostone has dedicated his life to cotton farming in Chinhoyi - the north-central capital of Zimbabwe’s Mashonaland West Province - despite market disturbances, climate change, and rising costs of input that threatened the crop.

Standing among cotton fields at a research farm in Kadoma along the road between Harare and Bulawayo, Bikostone tells the story of a cotton farming journey that has long hours of labour and perseverance despite global price fluctuations, which he describes as both a blessing and a challenge.

According to Stewart Mubonderi, the national chairman of the Cotton Producers and Marketers Association of Zimbabwe, the Zimbabwe Government has supported up to 400,000 cotton farmers at the household level, although this has reduced to 350,000 in recent years. Once one of Africa's leading cotton producers, Zimbabwe saw seed cotton production fall from a record 350,703 tonnes in 2010/11 to around 28,000–29,000 tonnes in 2025. The industry may now be turning a corner: the Agricultural Marketing Authority projects output of about 38,500 tonnes in 2026, raising hopes of a gradual revival.

Despite these challenges, cotton remains an important source of cash income for many rural households, particularly in areas where few alternative crops can thrive. The sector is now at a crossroads, with government and industry efforts focused on improving farmer returns, increasing production, rebuilding value chains, and restoring cotton's role as a driver of rural economic development and industrial growth.

“Cotton farming runs in my blood. For me to be who I am, it's cotton production. I have managed to send my four children to school, all of whom have now graduated. It has not been easy though, at one point, the dwindling prices (from US$1,35 to a paltry US$0,35 cents per kilogram) had an impact on my family,” says Bikostone.

“Imagine having spent so much money on the crop, and in return, there is nothing tangible. However, as time passed, I adjusted. As I said, cotton farming is rooted in me. I soldiered on, and I still produce a better crop year in, year out. With the coming of the hybrid seeds, our future looks bright,” said Bikostone

This veteran farmer’s different tune is thanks to a new generation of hybrid cotton seeds now available on the market. Unlike traditional seed varieties, hybrid seeds are developed by crossing two parent plants to combine desirable traits such as higher yields, improved drought tolerance, stronger resistance to pests and diseases, and more consistent performance in the field. For farmers facing increasingly unpredictable weather and rising production costs, these improved seeds are offering the prospect of better harvests and higher incomes.

“I had been using the Open-Pollinated Varieties (OPV), but after being introduced to the hybrid seed varieties, the yield has improved, and the cost of production is conducive. At first, I hesitated, and later on I embraced it, and it worked wonders. With enough support and viable prices, many farmers will return to cotton production because it can significantly improve household incomes,” said Bikostone.

His experience with hybrid seeds is part of a transformation in Zimbabwe's cotton industry, where stakeholders are collaborating to restore the crop to its status as white gold.

Tapiwa Bhiri, a Chinhoyi-based cottonseed breeder, says he started breeding the seed in 2025 and is delighted to be part of the cottonseed evolution.

“I joined the cottonseed breeding program last year. Cottonseed breeding requires monitoring to guarantee quality. During breeding, we use the 50 metres by 15 lines layout, which helps in maintaining quality. Today, I am happy because cotton farming has provided income to support my family and other projects outside farming,” said Bhiri.

Bikostone is not the only one who is seeing value in the hybrid seed, Arnold Gwengo, another farmer also from Chinhoyi, shared the same sentiments.

“With hybrid seeds you will never go wrong. I started using the varieties a few years ago and, honestly speaking, the results have been encouraging. One thing that is encouraging is that the hybrid seeds are resistant to pests and diseases,” said Gwengo.

Nyasha Gandiwa, Head of Research at Quton Seed Company, a leading supplier of cotton seed in Zimbabwe, says improved genetics are central to efforts to revive the country's struggling cotton sector. The company operates seed breeding and agronomy programmes from Kadoma and Harare and has been developing new hybrid varieties designed to boost yields while helping farmers cope with climate and pest pressures.

Ministry of Agriculture, Mechanisation and Water Resources Development Zim New Hope for Farmers as Govt Pushes Hybrid Seed and Fair Cotton Prices*

“We have new genetic technologies that we are developing, and some are already on the market,” Gandiwa said. “In Zimbabwe, cotton production has been on a downward spiral, and we are targeting to revitalize the cotton industry.”

According to Gandiwa, improved seed genetics account for a significant share of a farmer's potential productivity, although they must be combined with good farming practices to achieve the best results.

“In terms of research, genetics contribute about 50% of the final yield that the farmer gets, and the other 50% goes to crop management and crop husbandry practices that farmers get to use,” he said. “It is crucial that the farmer makes use of the best technologies available so that we improve farmer viability and yield.”

One of the main benefits of the new hybrid varieties, he said, is their ability to withstand increasingly challenging growing conditions while producing larger harvests.

“The advantages of these technologies are that they bring increased yield and are resistant to climate shocks and pests,” Gandiwa said.

He noted that while average cotton yields in Zimbabwe currently hover around 500 kilograms per hectare, farmers using improved varieties under good management conditions could achieve dramatically higher production levels.

“A farmer in Africa can achieve four or five tonnes per hectare, currently production figures in Zimbabwe in this current year we are talking about 500kgs per hectare,” he said.

The difference, Gandiwa argues, could be transformative for rural livelihoods.

“Using hybrid seeds we can actually have 4 tonnes per hectare. Imagine a farmer who was doing 500kg per hectare now does 4 tonnes that translates to good returns and the farmers’ livelihoods improves,” he said, adding that some of the new varieties can produce “up to 64 bolls per plant.”

Promotion Harutizwi, an agriculture extension officer from the Zimbabwe Farmers Union (ZFU), said hybrid seeds will play a critical role in the revitalization of the cotton industry.

“We have seen a great transformation from retained seeds to hybrid seeds. The good thing is hybrid seeds are resistant to pests and diseases which give high yields. They also don’t drop lint which gives high value market price as compared to the retained seeds. Hybrid seeds are critical in the revival of the cotton industry in the country and across Africa,” he said

Kaustubh Joshi, Quton Zimbabwe general manager, speaking at their hybrid cotton seed demonstration plot at a research farm in Kadoma, said the company’s objective was to revitalize the cotton industry in Zimbabwe and beyond.

“We are developing cotton seeds that we have taken to some parts of Africa and our aim is to develop climate smart seeds and resuscitate the cotton industry. Our objective is to produce seeds that bring high yields and also transform livelihoods for the farmers,” said Joshi

Chief Director of Agricultural and Rural Development Advisory Services (ARDAS) in Zimbabwe's Ministry of Agriculture, Mechanisation and Water Resources Development, Medlina Magwenzi, confirmed the government's commitment to restoring cotton production and the use of hybrid seed through research.

“We are realising that the cotton industry has been dwindling. But as a government, we know that this crop is just not a crop. It is a crop that we are looking forward to uplift the livelihoods of the smallholder farmers in Zimbabwe,” she said.

Magwenzi said the government is anchoring upon hybrid seed varieties to revive the industry.

“We want to make sure that we support this hybrid seed because hybrid seed will not only yield higher in the rain-fed fields… we want to make sure that we put a lot of water across these smallholder communities to make sure that we boost our yield. At the same time, we're also saying we are trying to put an enabling environment starting from seed production which should be genetically approved. We also want to make sure there is availability of fertilisers," Magwenzi said.

Asked what more can be done to incentivise farmers, she noted that markets had been a challenge for farmers and pricing needed to be dealt.

Zimbabwe's cotton revival is not being driven by fleets of tractors or vast mechanised farms. Instead, it begins with a tiny but powerful innovation inside a seed.

World.title: Multiple injured after floatplane makes emergency landing, catches fire off Washington coast
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Multiple people were injured Thursday after a Kenmore Air floatplane made an emergency landing off the Washington coast before catching fire, prompting a massive rescue operation, authorities said.

The U.S. Coast Guard said it received a report around 5:25 p.m. local time that a Kenmore Air seaplane had made an emergency landing in North Beach Shallow Bay off Sucia Island before bursting into flames.

Authorities said all 10 passengers and the pilot were accounted for.

SEN TIM SHEEHY MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER IN-FLIGHT ENGINE FAILURE

The San Juan County Sheriff's Office said multiple people suffered injuries ranging from head trauma to broken bones and lacerations.

Kenmore Air said four passengers were taken to local hospitals for treatment. Authorities said one person was in critical condition. No fatalities were immediately reported.

The airline said it was working closely with investigators and would provide additional updates as more information becomes available.

MISSOURI SKYDIVING PLANE CRASH THAT KILLED ALL 12 ABOARD IS A 'DEVASTATING LOSS,' COMPANY SAYS

Kenmore Air CEO David Gudgel said the company's immediate focus was on those aboard the aircraft.

"We are grateful that everyone aboard has been accounted for, and our immediate focus is ensuring our passengers and pilot receive the care and support they need," Gudgel said.

"We extend our sincere thanks to the United States Coast Guard, local emergency responders, and everyone assisting in the response," he continued. "Kenmore Air is fully cooperating with the investigating authorities, and we will continue providing verified information as it becomes available."

The airline said the aircraft involved was a de Havilland DHC-3 Otter operating near Sucia Island.

According to the sheriff's office, the flight departed Seattle's Lake Union and was headed to Roche Harbor Marina on San Juan Island.

A Kenmore Air spokesperson told Fox News Digital the route between Lake Union and the San Juan Islands is a routine flight for the airline.

"If you live here, you would be potentially taking a seaplane up there," the spokesperson said.

The U.S. Navy also responded, while three air ambulance helicopters transported injured passengers.

Orcas Island Fire & Rescue, Lopez Island Fire & Rescue, San Juan Island Fire & Rescue and San Juan County Parks also responded.

World.title: Former Fever player responds to Sophie Cunningham by alleging Indiana harassment cover-up
World.content:
The Indiana Fever are facing new scrutiny after former player Brianna Turner accused the organization of firing a male staff member over sexual harassment allegations during her time with the team, weighing in after Sophie Cunningham's comments on trans athletes.

Turner, a Fever player in 2025 and now with the Las Vegas Aces, made the allegations on X after Cunningham defended women's sports for biological females during an ESPN interview.

Cunningham said she wants to "protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men."

WHITE HOUSE DEFENDS WNBA STAR SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM AFTER SHE SPEAKS OUT IN SUPPORT OF PROTECTING WOMEN'S SPORTS

Turner barked at Cunningham's claims, saying organizations like the Fever are a greater threat to the game than trans athletes. According to Turner, the Fever fired a male staff member after allegations of sexual harassment but instructed players not to discuss the matter publicly.

She madly defended trans inclusion, pointing to former WNBA player Layshia Clarendon, who was born female before later identifying as transgender.

"To date there's been one out trans player in the league. They caused zero problems," Turner wrote on X.

WNBA PLAYER FACES BACKLASH OVER OP-ED CRITICIZING IOC FOR POLICY TO PROTECT WOMEN'S SPORTS

Turner contrasted that with the alleged conduct of the fired staff member, adding, "That is an issue. Sexism, misogyny, homophobia, and racism are all issues."

The Indiana Fever released a statement Thursday in response to Turner's claims.

"Protecting our players and employees and maintaining a respectful, professional workplace is our top priority," the Fever said.

"Our policy is to take concerns seriously, investigate thoroughly, and act promptly when appropriate to protect the people in our organization and ensure everyone is treated with professionalism and respect."

The team concluded, "Fostering trust and safety in that process means we do not comment on personnel matters involving former employees."

It remains unclear whether the WNBA will review Turner's allegations.

As of Thursday, the league had not announced an investigation or publicly commented.

World.title: California mayor's hot mic catches candid exchange after audience sends meeting off rails
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A live microphone exposed a behind-the-scenes conversation between Sacramento's mayor and vice mayor as they discussed whether disruptive protesters could be barred from future city council meetings after a heated immigration-related debate descended into chaos.

"We should go over this disruptions thing, because if we want to ban somebody in the future, like to take them out, we have to point out specifically…" Vice Mayor Karina Talamantes is heard saying.

"I know, but the city attorney said we can't do that," Mayor Kevin McCarty replied.

"We did it last time," Talamantes responded.

GOP SENATORS RALLY AROUND NEW DHS PROPOSAL TARGETING SANCTUARY CITIES: 'SHOULD PAY A PRICE'

"We can't," McCarty said, shaking his head. "I spent my first six months going over this. I wanted to give people, like, probation, like, you can't come…"

Talamantes then appeared to realize the microphone was still live and quickly reached over to switch it off before continuing the conversation, according to the publicly available city council livestream reviewed by Fox News Digital.

The awkward exchange unfolded Tuesday after Sacramento City Council recessed and ordered the public removed from the chambers following repeated disruptions during a fiery debate over the city's continued participation in a regional intelligence-sharing center.

The confrontation escalated after Talamantes defended accepting federal funding for the Central California Intelligence Center, or CCIC, arguing Sacramento's sanctuary city policies and immigrant protections made the city better suited to oversee the grant than other jurisdictions.

"The city of Sacramento is a sanctuary city," Talamantes said during the meeting. "If we don't pass these dollars, other counties will apply for these dollars, they will get those dollars and we will have no safeguards to protect our immigrant communities here in Sacramento."

Dozens of speakers had earlier urged the council to reject the agreement, arguing the intelligence center could facilitate information sharing with federal immigration authorities and undermine Sacramento's sanctuary city policies.

Police officials repeatedly disputed those claims during the meeting, telling council members Sacramento does not share personal identifying information for civil immigration enforcement and complies with California's sanctuary law, known as SB 54.

DHS LAWYER SAYS UCLA 'UTTERLY FAILED' TO STOP PROTEST CHAOS AT LAW SCHOOL APPEARANCE

As public comment grew increasingly heated, one speaker repeatedly demanded McCarty pay attention.

"Kevin, I need your f---ing eyes. Kevin, listen to me. Stop being an a--hole, dude. Listen to your f---ing constituents," the speaker shouted.

Following Talamantes' remarks, another round of shouting erupted inside the council chambers.

WATCH: HEARING DERAILS AS PURPLE-HAIRED DEM POINTS FINGER, SCREAMS AT CHAIR TO PUT DHS CHIEF 'IN HIS PLACE'

"You're a pick-me b----," one attendee shouted at Talamantes, while others yelled, "Shame on you."

McCarty responded with what he described as a "final notice."

"This is the final notice," the mayor said. "We're going to continue with the deliberation, and if there's any more outbursts, we're gonna have to ask the audience to leave."

Seconds later, the disruptions intensified.

"You can't do this behind closed f---ing doors!" one attendee shouted.

"We are the community," another yelled.

"You represent us. You are our f---ing audience," another voice exclaimed as council members attempted to continue the meeting.

Council officials then paused the meeting and cleared the chambers after repeated disruptions prevented deliberations from continuing.

Following the meeting, McCarty said the private conversation focused on existing meeting procedures, not new restrictions.

"Every Tuesday, Vice Mayor Talamantes and I are responsible for overseeing and ensuring transparent, accessible, and open Council meetings," McCarty said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"Unfortunately, when meetings are repeatedly disrupted, we must discuss existing policies and rules to ensure Council meetings remain effective, orderly, and respectful for both the residents in attendance and the Councilmembers. We are committed to ensuring that all members of the public can access and engage safely without distraction or intimidation."

The Sacramento City Attorney's Office declined to address McCarty's reference to legal advice during the hot-mic exchange.

"The City Attorney's Office has no comment and will not be providing comment on this matter," the office said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

The city's published meeting rules state that members of the public receive two minutes per agenda item and may speak on no more than four items during a meeting, limits intended to help the council conduct city business.

The hot-mic exchange quickly drew criticism from some activists, who argued Talamantes appeared interested in silencing vocal opponents.

Joshua Masias, a volunteer organizer with the Sac Immigration Committee, told The Sacramento Bee the conversation showed an authoritative approach toward members of the public.

"It's very authoritative how she wants to use her power," Masias told the outlet. "It stuck out to me that she was the only one to try to silence the crowd."

Resident Leanna Hunt, one of the council's most outspoken critics, also defended the protesters' frustration.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"I'm fed up," Hunt told the Bee. "It's not even a tactic — I'm just tired of being treated like we are an audience and that the king is deigning to see us peasants today and when the peasants are unruly, the king gets upset."

Fox News Digital reached out to Vice Mayor Talamantes' office, Sacramento Police Department and the Sac Immigration Committee for additional comment.

World.title: ESPN's Adam Schefter weighs in on LeBron James' NBA future after Heat press conference post sparks buzz
World.content:

LeBron James made it clear last month that retirement was not yet in his plans. The four-time NBA MVP said he plans to keep playing in 2026-27, but not with the Los Angeles Lakers.

Sixteen years ago, James placed his free agency at the center of a nationally televised spectacle. "The Decision," a special tied to his work with the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, ended with James revealing he would leave the Cleveland Cavaliers for the Miami Heat.

James left Miami in 2014 to return to his home state of Ohio, where he ultimately delivered the Cavaliers their first NBA title in 2016. He changed teams again in 2018, joining the Lakers.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

More recently, speculation has surfaced that James could be eyeing another return, this time to South Florida. Miami only fueled that talk earlier this week when it shared a since-deleted social media post linking to what was billed as the "LeBron James Introductory Press Conference."

A Heat team spokesperson later told ESPN the purported livestream event was not legitimate.

"I haven't read anything about, I haven't spoken to (anyone about it). But my guess would be where there's smoke, there's fire," ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter said in about the link in question.

AGENT RICH PAUL SAYS LEBRON JAMES WON'T BE RUSHED ON NBA FREE AGENCY DECISION DESPITE OUTSIDE PRESSURE

Schefter’s comments aligned with the growing speculation that James could land in Miami alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo next season.

"Had a text that said just be ready for LeBron to go to Miami. I can read you the exact text," Schefter continued during a recent appearance on Philadelphia's 97.5 The Fanatic. "‘I’m hearing Bron is coming to the Miami Heat, just want to give you a heads up. You may want to check it out.’"

Schefter pointed to a tip he said he received on June 30, when reports first surfaced that James would consider playing his 24th NBA season away from the Lakers.

The Cavaliers, Golden State Warriors and Philadelphia 76ers have also been linked to James.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

James remained productive last season, averaging 20.9 points, 7.2 assists, and 6.1 rebounds across 60 games. He remains the NBA’s all-time leading scorer.

World.title: Massachusetts Democratic Party chairman admits to sufficient facts in June drunken driving case
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The leader of the Massachusetts Democratic Party was arrested during a traffic stop on alleged drunken driving charges last month and days later admitted to prosecutors there were sufficient facts to support a conviction, according to state court records.

A judge on June 15 — two days after the traffic stop in the town of Southborough — continued the operating under the influence (OUI) liquor charge without a finding after Steve Kerrigan, chairman of the state's Democratic Party, entered an "admission to sufficient facts," a Massachusetts legal disposition in which a defendant acknowledges prosecutors have enough evidence to obtain a conviction, according to Westborough District Court records.

In addition to the OUI charge, Kerrigan, 54, faced a negligent operation charge and a marked lanes violation. The negligent operation charge was dismissed, and he was found not responsible for the marked lanes violation.

The judge sentenced Kerrigan to a year's probation, suspended his driver's license for 45 days, ordered him to pay $600 in fees and required him to complete an impaired driving education program.

COLORADO DEMOCRATS FORMALLY CENSURE GOV POLIS OVER TINA PETERS COMMUTATION

Kerrigan was elected chair of the Massachusetts Democratic Party in 2023. He was the Democratic nominee for lieutenant governor in 2014, and previously served as an executive with the Democratic National Convention Committee. He also serves as president and CEO of the Edward M. Kennedy Community Health Center.

According to a Southborough Police Department report, an officer stopped Kerrigan shortly after midnight on June 13, after observing his BMW traveling on or over the lane divider.

The officer wrote that Kerrigan's eyes appeared "glassy" and "bloodshot red" and that his speech was slow and slurred. The report states the officer could not detect the smell of alcohol because of what was described as an "overwhelming odor of cologne."

FLORIDA MAN ARRESTED FOR DUI AFTER TROOPERS ALLEGEDLY FIND 34 OPEN ALCOHOL CONTAINERS IN VEHICLE

Kerrigan told the officer he was driving home from a restaurant and said he had consumed two beers around 6 p.m. before dinner, according to the report.

Police administered field sobriety tests before Kerrigan provided a breath sample that registered a 0.089% blood alcohol content, according to the report. The legal blood alcohol limit in Massachusetts is 0.08%.

Kerrigan acknowledged the incident in a statement provided to Boston.com through his attorney, Andrea Levy.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"In June, I was pulled over for a marked lanes violation and blew a .089 on the breathalyzer," Kerrigan said. "I regret and take full responsibility for my actions and their consequences and appreciate the Southborough Police Department and the Westborough Court for their professionalism and service."

The Massachusetts Democratic Party did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

World.title: House votes to end Iran war, but Senate Republicans vote to let Trump continue waging it
World.content:
WASHINGTON — The House on Thursday approved a Democratic-led proposal to end the Iran war, directing President Donald Trump to remove armed forces from hostilities.

Subscribe to read this story ad-free Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

The resolution is nonbinding, however. The House voted 214-208, with four Republicans joining all Democrats to cast decisive votes for the measure: Reps. Thomas Massie of Kentucky, Tom Barrett of Michigan, Warren Davidson of Ohio and Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania.

Later in the day, the Senate voted 47-49 to reject a “joint resolution” to end the Iran war that would have the force of law, unlike the House version, but would be subject to a presidential veto. One Republican, Sen. Susan Collins of Maine, joined every Democrat except Sen. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania in voting to advance the measure.

Four Republicans didn’t vote: Sens. Katie Britt of Alabama, Mitch McConnell of Kentucky, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and Rand Paul of Kentucky.

The votes in both chambers were pushed by Democrats eager to get Republicans on the record about an unpopular war ahead of the midterm elections and to reassert Congress’ role as the branch of government responsible for declaring war.

Multiple Senate Republicans have said the war should not go on for more than 60 days without congressional approval in order to comply with federal law. They include Sens. Thom Tillis of North Carolina and John Curtis of Utah. But both men on Thursday voted against the measure to end the Iran war.

Asked why, Tillis said the 60-day clock started this month, not back in February when Trump and Israel first launched strikes on Iran. “July 10, to my knowledge, is the first time I heard anyone in the administration refer to it as a war,” Tillis said, adding that it would be important for Congress to authorize the war once 60 days are up.

“The clock is ticking. We got to get serious about that,” Tillis said. “I think politically, we can help the president with an unpopular war right now if we provide some legitimacy to it.”

House Republicans have also indicated their willingness to give Trump breathing room on the 60-day deadline. Still, four GOP members voted with Democrats to pass the nonbinding resolution rejecting the war through the Republican-controlled House, reflecting the unpopularity of the conflict.

“The vote today shows that Congress is starting to join the 70% of American people who are against this war, which is clearly a war of choice, and Congress has to step up to our constitutional responsibility and demand it,” Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, told NBC News.

Meeks added that Democrats have more tools to force Trump to end the war, such as the “power of the purse” ahead of a Sept. 30 deadline for Congress to fund the government, including the military. He added that he’s introducing a resolution “to sue the administration,” accusing it of defying Congress on the Iran war, which he plans to force a vote on when the House returns from its summer recess in five weeks.

Public opposition to the Iran war has put Republicans in competitive areas in a difficult position.

Rep. Rob Bresnahan, R-Pa., who represents a swing district and is a top target of Democrats in November, voted against the resolution. He said he recognizes the war’s economic impact but emphasized that Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon.

“I think people see the prices of fuel and they immediately correlate one and the other. But I think we’re all in agreement that this needs to come to a resolution expeditiously. Under no circumstances should Iran have nuclear weapons,” Bresnahan said Thursday. “Iran is not a friend to the United States, but there needs to be a definitive solution there quickly.”

He said he’d like the Strait of Hormuz to open as soon as possible so the prices of gas and fertilizer can come back down. “The sooner, the better,” he said. “But at the same time, you can’t allow a foreign adversary to run rogue and hold hostage American supply chains because ... they are just acting radically.”

Seven Republicans and two Democrats didn’t cast a vote on the House’s Iran measure Thursday.

It is not the first time that Congress has formally disapproved of the war. The House approved a similar war powers resolution in early June on a 215-208 vote, with the same Republicans supporting it who voted for the measure Thursday. The Senate later passed the same nonbinding measure.

Democrats have continued to force these votes to get Republicans on the record about a war that a majority of Americans oppose. The failed Senate measure was led by Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md.

“Not only are the vast majority of Americans opposed to this war; it’s the most unpopular war that we’ve had in a very, very, very long time,” Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., said, noting that even self-identified “MAGA” voters are skeptical of the war.

“These are folks who deeply support Donald Trump, but they actually liked when he was talking about ending forever wars instead of getting into them,” she said.

World.title: Justice Department agrees to withdraw subpoenas of New York Times journalists over Air Force One reporting
World.content:
The Justice Department agreed Thursday to withdraw grand jury subpoenas seeking testimony and records from New York Times reporters and their family members after a federal judge repeatedly questioned why prosecutors had issued the subpoenas before they pursued alternative investigative steps.

Subscribe to read this story ad-free Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

At a hearing Thursday before U.S. District Judge Arun Subramanian in Manhattan, prosecutor Sean Buckley initially resisted withdrawing the subpoenas, arguing that they should instead be held in abeyance so the government could preserve the records in case they were needed later.

But Subramanian repeatedly pressed Buckley about the distinction, noting that the government could quash the subpoenas and return to court later with new applications if justified.

“Doesn’t the law indicate that subpoenas are the last step? Not the first step but the last step?” Subramanian repeatedly asked.

“Subpoenas issued to reporters for their records, they are not the first thing you do; they are the last thing you do,” he added, citing the “profound First Amendment issues” involved.

Buckley acknowledged that the government had mistakenly obtained phone records associated with the reporters’ relatives, including spouses and, in one instance, a reporter’s mother, after a public-source database incorrectly linked the numbers to the subject of the investigation.

“That was an error,” Buckley said. “It was a mistake; it was not in furtherance of the investigation.”

The Trump administration initially subpoenaed a group of Times reporters a few weeks ago after the paper published articles about security concerns surrounding the new Air Force One, which was donated by Qatar.

The stories came out after President Donald Trump flew home from an international trip to Turkey on the old Air Force One, prompting questions about why the new aircraft wasn’t used.

The Times journalists, using anonymous sources, reported that the Secret Service urged Trump to fly home on the old presidential aircraft after a resumption of hostilities with Iran, partially because the new Air Force One isn’t equipped with antimissile capabilities.

The paper said at the time that some of the subpoenas were issued to reporters by federal agents who showed up at their homes and that the subpoenas sought information about who leaked details about the security concerns to the reporters.

In a statement, David McGraw, the Times’ senior vice president and deputy general counsel, called the Justice Department’s decision to drop the subpoenas “an important affirmation of our country’s commitment to a free press.”

He added: “We are pleased that the government finally conceded that the subpoenas violated the law, but they should never have been issued in the first place. The Times and our journalists will continue to report and seek the truth without fear or favor. We will not be deterred in the face of tactics like these.”

A Justice Department spokesperson blamed Subramanian in a statement, saying: “This judge threatened our attorneys with sanctions unless subpoenas were withdrawn, and blocked us from presenting the meticulous process of this investigation. The grand jury has a right to hear testimony from all material witnesses in a federal criminal investigation. This judge’s conduct overrides clear longstanding principles and common sense—blocking the grand jury from receiving core evidence in a national security investigation.”

The spokesperson added that the investigation continues.

Buckley said Thursday that the reporters aren’t the targets of the investigation, the leakers are, and that the government is prepared to immunize them to compel their testimony.

Subramanian also warned that the government’s incorrect and incomplete court submissions could lead to sanctions, saying that in a civil case he would normally require the parties to show cause why sanctions shouldn’t be imposed for misstatements to the court. Buckley called the errors inadvertent.

The government ultimately agreed to withdraw the subpoenas and pursue other investigative steps while reserving the possibility of seeking new subpoenas in the future.

Times attorney David O’Neil said the newspaper fundamentally disagreed with the government’s argument that holding the subpoenas in abeyance was equivalent to withdrawing them.

“There are fundamental First Amendment issues. The record is replete with bad faith,” O’Neil said, adding that the subpoenas had already had a chilling effect on the reporters.

“Given the chill these subpoenas have already produced, it is clear that having these subpoenas out there has been damaging to the reporters,” he said.

O’Neil also emphasized that the government had acted unilaterally in issuing the subpoenas and seeking the phone records.

Subramanian ended the hearing on a light note, asking prosecutors whether someone is at home watching the new movie starring Hugh Jackman, “Sheep Detectives.”

“We are not going to have FBI agents showing up at the door?” he asked after referring to the movie, with Justice Department attorneys promising that won’t be happening.
