World.title: ICC members to vote on dismissing prosecutor Khan
World.content:
Prosecutor Karim Khan denies any wrongdoing and his lawyers call the decision by the court's governing body procedurally unfair and unsupported by evidence

THE HAGUE, Netherlands – International Criminal Court member states are set to vote on Friday, July 24, on whether to dismiss the court’s chief prosecutor Karim Khan for alleged sexual misconduct.

Khan, 56, denies any wrongdoing and his lawyers have called the decision by the court’s governing body that led to Friday’s vote unlawful, procedurally unfair and unsupported by evidence.

The vote comes amid renewed US criticism of the war crimes court which Washington sees as a threat to its sovereignty.

If ICC member states dismiss Khan, it will be seen by his supporters as the result of political pressure after the prosecutor sought arrest warrants for senior Israeli officials for alleged war crimes committed in Gaza. Israel denies war crimes, is not a member of the court and has dismissed the warrants as bogus.

Even if Khan survives the vote, his position would be weakened and it would give critics of the court — established in 2002 by the international community to prosecute war crimes, genocide and crimes against humanity — another stick to beat it with.

Rubio decries ‘lunatics’ at the court

During a visit to the Philippines on Thursday, July 23, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there were “lunatics and crazies involved in the ICC” and there was no way any US political or military officials would ever go on trial at the court, reiterating previous criticism.

The US, which is also not a member, has already imposed sanctions on 11 ICC judges and prosecutors, including Khan, citing the ICC’s arrest warrants against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defense minister Yoav Gallant, and a past probe into US troops in Afghanistan.

Officials from the court’s governing body have said Khan should be dismissed because he committed serious misconduct by having an inappropriate sexual relationship with a junior staff member, according to documents seen by Reuters.

For Khan to be fired, an absolute majority of at least 63 of the court’s 125 member states will have to agree in the secret ballot to be held at a meeting at the UN headquarters in New York. The vote is due around 3 pm (1900 GMT) and the result is expected to be announced at 5:30 pm (2130 GMT).

France said on Thursday it would vote in favor of the removal of Khan, who has been suspended since June, after being on voluntary leave since May 2025 while awaiting the outcome of the internal investigation.

The Netherlands, which hosts the court in The Hague, has also said it would support his dismissal.

Election process begins if Khan removed

Khan’s accuser, a junior ICC staffer, spoke publicly for the first time last week in an interview with CNN in which she repeated her allegations that the prosecutor had a nonconsensual sexual relationship with her.

Lawyers for Khan told Reuters he denied “any sexual relationship of any kind” with the staff member.

If Khan is fired, that would immediately trigger the election process for a new ICC prosecutor who is not expected to be voted in before next year.

Any active ICC warrants will remain in place even if Khan is dismissed because only ICC judges have the authority to withdraw warrants. – Rappler.com

World.title: FACT CHECK: NBI agent Calilung not arrested after VP Sara trial testimony
World.content:
There is no warrant or report of an arrest made after NBI agent John Mark Calilung testified as the first witness in the Vice President's impeachment trial

Claim: Senior National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) agent John Mark Calilung, the first witness in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, has been arrested.

Rating: FALSE

Why we fact-checked this: A YouTube channel named “PHILIPPINES TRENDING NEWS” uploaded a video containing the claim on July 12.

The video is titled “Kinarma na! Kakapasok lang, matinding utos, Senado, pirmado na? Wala [nang] takas; huli, NBI witness kulong?”

(Karma has struck! Just in: Major Senate order signed? No escape, NBI witness caught, jailed?)

Its thumbnail, which shows images of Calilung and Duterte, also bears the text, “Kulong na ngayon lang, NBI witness, arestado na?” (Jailed just now? NBI witness already arrested?)

As of writing, the video has garnered over 28,000 views and 1,100 likes.

The facts: Calilung was never arrested or jailed following his testimony before the Senate impeachment court on July 7 and the cross-examination by one of Duterte’s defense counsel, Carlo Narvasa, on July 8. The NBI agent was not detained by authorities nor was an arrest warrant issued for him right after his appearance at the trial.

The video’s central claim is also unsupported by its own content. Rather than presenting evidence that Calilung was arrested, the video recycles political commentary from Duterte-aligned political vlogger Banat By, largely talking about Calilung’s testimony and questioning his credibility.

At no point does the narration claim or discuss that Calilung had been arrested or detained.

The first witness: Calilung served as the prosecution’s primary witness to authenticate a November 2024 video from a press conference held by the Duterte, in which she allegedly made grave threats against the President. These form the basis of Article IV of the impeachment complaint against her.

As an officer of the NBI’s Cybercrime Division, Calilung explained how investigators preserved and authenticated footage in which Duterte allegedly said that, should anything happen to her, an assassin was prepared to kill President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and then-House speaker Martin Romualdez. (READ: Sara Duterte: If I get killed, so will Marcos, Liza Araneta, Romualdez)

During cross-examination, Duterte’s defense questioned Calilung’s qualifications as a digital forensic examiner, prompting Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero to direct Calilung to submit his certifications.

The grave threats charge is one of four articles of impeachment against Duterte. The others allege the misuse of confidential and intelligence funds, culpable violation of the Constitution and betrayal of public trust — including allegations of unexplained wealth — and bribery and corruption. – Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com

Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

World.title: China uses water cannons on Philippine ships 2 days in a row
World.content:
WATER CANNONS AGAIN. A China Coast Guard ships uses water cannons against a PCG vessel in Bajo de Masinloc on Friday, July 24.

Another Philippine mission to Bajo de Masinloc in the West Philippine Sea is met with the China Coast Guard’s water cannons just as high-level ASEAN events in Manila wrap up

MANILA, Philippines — At least three Philippine vessels were hit by water cannons from their Chinese counterparts during a mission to Bajo de Masinloc (Scarborough Shoal) on Friday morning, July 24. It was the second straight day that the China Coast Guard used water cannons against Philippine vessels near the feature, which Beijing has controlled access to since 2012.

In a release, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) said two CCG ships hit the PCG’s BRP Cape San Agustin and the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) vessel BRP Datu Paduhinog within an hour and a half of each other Friday, between 6:26 am and 7:53 am.

The Philippine ships were sailing as close as 10 to 15 nautical miles away from Bajo de Masinloc, a high-tide elevation just over 100 nautical miles from the Philippine mainland.

Before 9 am on Friday, a CCG ship trained its water cannon on another BFAR vessel, BRP Datu Cabaylo.

The CCG ships also used dangerous manuevers on — or sailed dangerously and aggressively close to — the Philippine vessels.

The PCG said a Chinese Maritime Militia ship was monitored “pulling a rope” some 100 meters ahead of the BFAR’s BRP Datu Sumakwel, “[posing] a hazard to the vessel’s safe navigation.”

The PCG said personnel were safe and the vessels went ahead with their mission to bring fuel subsidies and provisions to Filipino fisherfolk in the area.

As of 9:30 am, there were at least 12 CCG vessels and 3 Chinese Maritime Militia ships. The Philippines, meanwhile, deployed 3 PCG ships and 7 BFAR vessels.

“The PCG strongly condemns the dangerous and unprofessional actions of the China Coast Guard. Bajo de Masinloc is an integral part of the Philippine territory, and its surrounding waters form part of the country’s territorial sea and exclusive economic zone. The 2016 Arbitral Award has affirmed that Bajo de Masinloc is a traditional fishing ground of Filipino fisherfolk, whose rights cannot be lawfully impeded by any foreign power,” said the PCG.

Just a day prior, on July 23, the CCG also used water cannons on PCG and BFAR ships.

It’s been a week of tense confrontations between the Philippines and China in the West Philippine Sea, a part of the South China Sea that includes the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone (EEZ).

On July 20, CCG personnel entered Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal, where the rusting BRP Sierra Madre has been aground since 1999. A tense confrontation between the CCG and Philippine soldiers led to the injuries, including a head wound on one Filipino.

The Philippines and China have traded protests over the Ayungin incident, including during a bilateral meeting between their foreign ministers on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) meetings in Manila. – Rappler.com

World.title: Tropical Storm Kiyapo strengthens further near Cagayan
World.content:
KIYAPO. Satellite image of Tropical Storm Kiyapo (Noul) as of July 24, 2026, 10 am.

Tropical Storm Kiyapo (Noul) is projected to pass very close to or make landfall in Cagayan's Babuyan Islands on Friday, July 24

MANILA, Philippines – Tropical Storm Kiyapo (Noul) slightly intensified on Friday morning, July 24, as it moved closer to extreme Northern Luzon.

Kiyapo’s maximum sustained winds increased from 65 kilometers per hour to 75 km/h, said the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) in its 11 am bulletin on Friday. The tropical storm’s gustiness is now up to 90 km/h from the previous 80 km/h.

Kiyapo also accelerated, moving west at 30 km/h from 20 km/h. It was already 135 kilometers east of Aparri, Cagayan, as of 10 am on Friday.

In the coming hours, the tropical storm will be passing close to the northeastern portion of mainland Cagayan, then passing very close to or making landfall in Cagayan’s Babuyan Islands.

Kiyapo may also strengthen further into a severe tropical storm after passing the Babuyan Islands, followed by potential rapid intensification over the West Philippine Sea, where it could become a typhoon.

PAGASA’s latest rainfall advisory for Kiyapo, also issued at 11 am on Friday, shows moderate to intense rain may persist in Northern Luzon in the next 24 hours.

Friday noon, July 24, to Saturday noon, July 25

Heavy to intense rain (100-200 millimeters): Batanes, Cagayan, Apayao, Ilocos Norte

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Isabela, Kalinga, Abra, Benguet, Ilocos Sur, La Union

Meanwhile, moderate to heavy rain from the southwest monsoon or habagat could continue in several provinces on the western side of the country within 48 hours.

Friday noon, July 24, to Saturday noon, July 25

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Occidental Mindoro, Palawan, Antique, Iloilo, Guimaras, Negros Occidental

Saturday noon, July 25, to Sunday noon, July 26

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Bataan, Occidental Mindoro

Affected areas must remain on alert for floods and landslides.

With Kiyapo moving closer to extreme Northern Luzon, some areas were upgraded to Signal No. 2 at 11 am on Friday. These are all the areas under tropical cyclone wind signals:

Signal No. 2

Gale-force winds (62 to 88 km/h), minor to moderate threat to life and property

Batanes

northern part of Cagayan (Santa Ana, Gonzaga, Santa Teresita, Camalaniugan, Aparri, Ballesteros, Abulug, Pamplona, Sanchez-Mira, Claveria, Santa Praxedes, Buguey, Allacapan, Lal-lo, Gattaran, Baggao, Lasam) including Babuyan Islands

northern part of Apayao (Luna, Santa Marcela, Calanasan, Pudtol, Flora)

northern part of Ilocos Norte (Pagudpud, Dumalneg, Adams, Bangui, Burgos, Vintar)

Signal No. 1

Strong winds (39 to 61 km/h), minimal to minor threat to life and property

rest of mainland Cagayan

Isabela

Quirino

Nueva Vizcaya

rest of Apayao

Abra

Kalinga

Mountain Province

Ifugao

Benguet

rest of Ilocos Norte

Ilocos Sur

La Union

northern and central parts of Aurora (Dilasag, Casiguran, Dinalungan, Dipaculao)

PAGASA might raise Signal No. 3 if Kiyapo becomes a severe tropical storm while crossing the Batanes-Babuyan Islands area.

The southwest monsoon and Kiyapo’s periphery or outer bands are also bringing strong to gale-force gusts to these areas:

Friday, July 24

most of the country

Saturday, July 25

most of Luzon, most of Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Davao Oriental

Sunday, July 26

Ilocos Region, Mimaropa, Zambales, Bataan, Quezon

Moreover, moderate to very rough sea conditions persist in seaboards affected by Kiyapo and the southwest monsoon.

Up to very rough seas (travel is risky for all vessels)

Seaboards of Batanes and Babuyan Islands – waves up to 5.5 meters high

Northern seaboards of mainland Cagayan and Ilocos Norte – waves up to 4.5 meters high

Up to rough seas (small vessels should not venture out to sea)

Remaining seaboards of mainland Cagayan and Ilocos Norte; northeastern seaboard of Isabela; northern seaboard of Ilocos Sur; eastern seaboard of Davao Oriental – waves up to 3 meters high

Up to moderate to rough seas (small vessels should take precautionary measures or avoid sailing, if possible)

Seaboards of Zambales and Surigao del Sur; northern seaboard of Aurora; western seaboard of Pangasinan; remaining seaboards of Isabela and Ilocos Sur – waves up to 2.5 meters high

Seaboards of Cuyo Islands, Kalayaan Islands, Cagayancillo Islands, and Davao Occidental; northern seaboards of La Union, Camarines Norte, and Camarines Sur; northern and eastern seaboards of Polillo Islands and Catanduanes; eastern seaboards of Albay, Sorsogon, Northern Samar, Eastern Samar, Dinagat Islands, and Siargao-Bucas Grande Islands; western seaboards of Bataan, Occidental Mindoro including Lubang Islands, mainland Palawan including Calamian Islands and Negros Occidental; southern seaboards of Antique, Iloilo, Guimaras, Negros Oriental, Davao Oriental, and Sarangani; remaining seaboard of Aurora – waves up to 2 meters high

Kiyapo is the Philippines’ 11th tropical cyclone for 2026, and the fourth for July alone. It may exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility by Saturday morning, July 25, then head for China. – Rappler.com

World.title: LIST: SONA 2026 protests, activities in PH and overseas
World.content:
Here are events and initiatives organized by progressive groups, civil society organizations, and business groups ahead of SONA 2026

MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is set to deliver his fifth State of the Nation Address (SONA) on Monday, July 27.



Various groups are coming together to amplify sectoral concerns and encourage public engagement in the lead-up to and on the day of the SONA.

These activities include protests, community gatherings, forums, cultural events, and more, both in the Philippines and abroad. Below is a list of these activities:

Refresh this page for updates as more event details are announced.

Protests

A day before SONA, on Sunday, July 26, the Kabataan Partylist–National Capital Region will hold a State of the Youth Address 2026 at the IFI National Cathedral Conference Hall, Manila.

The ceremony will gather youth groups, student councils, campus publications, organizations, and student leaders from Metro Manila to raise calls on education, accountability, and social concerns, as young advocates assert their role in shaping the country’s future.

Meanwhile, around 10,000 protesters are expected to converge outside the Batasang Pambansa on Monday, July 27, as the Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (BAYAN) and its allied people’s organizations stage their annual People’s State of the Nation Address.

The program will begin at 12 pm along Commonwealth Avenue, followed by a 2 pm march to Saint Peter Parish, where multisectoral groups will hold what they describe as the country’s “real state of the nation.”

Panday Sining UP Diliman will be preparing for the protest through banner and effigy-making operations at the Student Union Building (SUB) in UP Diliman, Quezon City from July 15 to July 25.

The Philippine Medical Students’ Association is also recruiting volunteer medics for the People’s SONA, calling on medical and health science students to provide first aid during the mobilization.

Forums

Quezon City | The UP National College of Public Administration and Governance (NCPAG) is conducting a forum titled, “SONA ALL! Stocktaking of PBBM’s SONA Promises from 2022-2025” on Friday, July 24 at the UP NCPAG AVR in Diliman, Quezon City from 1 pm to 5 pm. The discussion aims to examine the promises made by Marcos during past SONAs.



The UP National College of Public Administration and Governance (NCPAG) is conducting a forum titled, “SONA ALL! Stocktaking of PBBM’s SONA Promises from 2022-2025” on Friday, July 24 at the UP NCPAG AVR in Diliman, Quezon City from 1 pm to 5 pm. The discussion aims to examine the promises made by Marcos during past SONAs. Online Gabriela Youth – Muntinlupa and Kabataan Partylist – Muntinlupa is organizing a discussion on “Flood and Blood: The Cost of Corruption” at 1 pm on Friday, July 24, to tackle the critical national developments surrounding public accountability in the context of the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte and the core issues of President Marcos’ SONA.

The European Chamber Commerce of the Philippines (ECCP) is organizing the “ECCP Post-SONA Business and Policy Analysis” on Tuesday, July 28, from 2 pm to 4 pm to provide post-SONA insights into the President’s key policy directions and their implications for businesses, investments, and different industries.



Local, sectoral activities

Quezon City

Indigenous women from 20 communities across the Philippines will gather for the National Indigenous Women Gathering 2026 from July 25 to 29. Led by LILAK (Purple Action for Indigenous Women’s Rights), the gathering will consolidate calls for accountability and justice over the plunder of resources and the continuing attacks on land and environment women human rights defenders. Participants will cap the gathering by joining the mobilization on July 27 and holding a community watch party in the afternoon. LILAK is also leading an alliance of progressive groups alongside Alyansa Tigil Mina (ATM) and In Defense of Human Rights and Dignity Movement (IDEFEND), for a protest action outside the Department of Environment and Natural Resources Central Office on Monday, July 27, at 9 am, calling for accountability over corruption, environmental destruction, and policies they say have deepened poverty. Vandals United is staging a “Streets of the Nation Attack” protest with a community of skaters, graffiti artists, writers, and musicians at the Commission on Human Rights, Commonwealth Avenue, Quezon City on Monday, July 27, at 9 am. It aims to highlight issues of poverty, education, job security, land grabbing, and workers’ rights under the current administration.



Lapu-Lapu City | The Concerned Artists of the Philippines (CAP) Cebu Chapter is hosting an exhibition from July 24 until August 14 at the Lapu-Lapu Art Gallery. Dubbed, “Same Old, Same Old: The State of the Nation, the exhibition brings together works from four political poster exhibitions mounted between 2023 and 2026, revisiting campaigns and artistic responses to issues affecting ordinary Filipinos.

World.title: FACT CHECK: VP Sara did not flee PH due to death of Caloocan vlogger
World.content:
The Office of the Vice President says Duterte's scheduled trip and activities in different countries in Europe are intended to engage with overseas Filipinos

Claim: Vice President Sara Duterte has left the country after the Philippine National Police (PNP) identified the suspects behind the death of a vlogger known by her online name “Mima Alicia.”

Rating: MISSING CONTEXT

Why we fact-checked this: The claim was posted by Facebook page Balita at Kaalaman on July 21. The post has now gained more than 4,100 reactions and 1,300 comments as of writing.

The post reads “Breaking News: Sara Duterte umalis ng bansa, ‘yan ay pagkatapos matukoy ng #PNP ang mga salarin sa pagtegi kay #MimaAlicia. Takot ba siyang ituro ng mga hitman? #JusticeForMimaAlicia”

(Breaking news: Sara Duterte has left the country after the PNP identified the suspect behind the death of Mima Alicia. Is she afraid that the hitman will point fingers at her? #JusticeForMimaAlicia)

The post was referring to the July 17 killing of the vlogger known for her support for the Marcos administration and being critical of Duterte. It seems to suggest that the Vice President’s travel was linked to the vlogger’s death.

The comments section of the post received mixed reactions. Some social media users criticized the Vice President for the timing of her departure as her impeachment trial is ongoing. Others questioned the credibility of the page, suggesting that the page’s administrators are allegedly among the paid trolls by the Marcos administration.

The facts: Duterte did, in fact, leave the country. However, her overseas trip from July 16 to 31 was for meetings with overseas Filipinos and personal engagements, according to the Office of the Vice President (OVP) — a fact that the misleading post failed to disclose.

Her travel will include stops in Qatar, Germany, the United Kingdom, Northern Ireland, and the Netherlands to meet with Filipino migrant workers and attend a forum.

“These activities are intended to engage with overseas Filipinos and advance the Philippines’ interests abroad,” the OVP said in a statement on July 21.

“The itinerary includes both official foreign travel and personal engagements. No government funds will be used by the Vice President for the entire duration of the trip,” the OVP added.

The Vice President’s trip came amid her ongoing impeachment trial. Duterte is the only public official in the country’s history to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives. She is accused of alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery of Department of Education officials, and grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.

Mima Alicia’s death: Political vlogger Alicia Lipata, known as “Mima Alicia,” was killed by two motorcycle-riding gunmen outside her home in Caloocan City on July 17.

Based on investigations, the Northern Police District is currently looking at the possibility that her death is linked to her political commentary.

Lipata was known to be supportive of the administration of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and a critic of Duterte and her allies.

On July 23, police said the two suspects behind Lipata’s death have been arrested and are set to face murder charges. Authorities are still investigating the motive behind the killing. – Lourence Angelo Marcellana/Rappler.com

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

World.title: WATCH: Red flag or green flag? Advocates weigh in on anti-disinformation bill
World.content:
In this video, the Ateneo Human Rights Center, Youth Voices Count, PressOne, and PHINMA Education evaluate the critical provisions of the bill and decide whether they are ready to commit, or pop the red balloon

MANILA, Philippines – If a piece of legislation were a dating profile, would you swipe right, or is it a total red flag?



Ahead of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s State of the Nation Address (SONA), the House of Representatives approved House Bill No. 9465, or the proposed Digital Media Anti-False Information Act.

The bill seeks to penalize the intentional spread of online falsehoods that cause verifiable public harm or threaten national security. On paper, the measure carries several “green flags” that free speech and transparency advocates welcome. It also attempts to mandate tech giants like Facebook and TikTok to undergo annual independent audits, publicly disclose political ads, and work with education agencies to institutionalize media literacy across all school levels.

Despite the assurance of lawmakers, including the bill’s principal author House Majority Leader Sandro Marcos, that the bill shields the public from malicious online deception, the proposed measure drew concerns from civil society organizations and media advocates.

To weigh in on this new bill, #FactsFirstPH, a multi-stakeholder coalition of truth-tellers and advocates, subjected the bill to a simulated “dating show” assessment.

In the video, the Ateneo Human Rights Center, Youth Voices Count, PressOne, and PHINMA Education evaluate the critical provisions of the bill and decide whether they are ready to commit, or pop the red balloon.

A Senate version of an anti-disinformation bill is also being debated, but this is not tackled in this video. #FactsFirstPH joined over 50 media organizations in a joint statement about the Senate and House anti-disinformation bills. Read the full statement here.

In the past, the coalition also spearheaded multi-sectoral fact-checking initiatives to combat systemic election propaganda, monitored coordinated inauthentic behavior and disinformation networks, and provided legal safeguards for truth-tellers under attack.

Know more about the bill by reading why censorship fears linger despite the revisions and understand what’s at stake.

Join the #FactsFirstPH coalition by emailing moveph@rappler.com. – Rappler.com

HEIGHTENED ALERT. Officers of the Police Regional Office-10 march in formation during a pass in review in Cagayan de Oro City. Photo courtesy of PRO-10

CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — Assuring the public that the right to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly will be firmly protected, the Police Regional Office-10 (PRO-10) announced the strategic deployment of 4,688 personnel across Northern Mindanao ahead of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr’s fifth State of the Nation Address (Sona) on Monday, July 27.

“While the Philippine National Police remains steadfast in upholding every citizen’s right to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly, we call on the participants to exercise these rights responsibly and within the bounds of the law,” Brig. Gen. Christopher Abrahano, PRO-10 commander, said in a press advisory on Friday, July 24.

To maintain order while the President delivers his address at the Batasang Pambansa Complex in Quezon City, the entire PRO-10 force has been placed on heightened alert. The deployed officers are positioned to secure vital installations, transportation hubs, major thouroughfares, and other critical places of convergence throughout the region.

Article continues after this 

READ: PNP sees no security threat to Marcos’ 5th Sona

Maj. Joann Navarro, PRO-10 spokesperson, told the Inquirer that police commanders throughout the region have been directed to intensify visibility, sustain intelligence monitoring, and coordinate closely with force multipliers and partner agencies to tighten public security.

World.title: Landslide cuts off another Bukidnon-Davao road link
World.content:
Debris, rocks, and uprooted trees cover a 35-meter stretch of the concrete highway at Sitio Sapiki in Paquibato District, Davao City, following a landslide triggered by heavy rains on July 23. The incident rendered the road connecting San Fernando, Bukidnon, to Davao City and Panabo, Davao del Norte, impassable to all vehicles and left several motorists stranded. PHOTO BY ADELINO ESPELITA GOCOTANO

VALENCIA CITY, Bukidnon — Heavy rains triggered a landslide on Thursday afternoon that rendered impassable to all vehicles a major road network connecting San Fernando, Bukidnon to Davao City.

The affected stretch—which passes through the villages of Kalagangan, Cabuling, Durian, and Matupi in San Fernando toward Davao City’s Paquibato District and Panabo, Davao del Norte—was shut down after debris buried the concrete road around 3:00 p.m. on July 23.

READ: Clearing of landslide debris from Bukidnon road may take 4 months

Article continues after this 

Anthony Sindoy of the San Fernando Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (DRRMO) said an initial assessment showed that roughly 30 to 35 meters of earth, rocks, and uprooted trees covered the highway at Sitio Sapiki in Paquibato District, stranding several motorists.

Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Region 11 spokesperson Dean Ortiz confirmed Friday that engineers are currently evaluating the site to launch clearing operations as soon as conditions permit.

Meanwhile, clearing efforts continue at a separate landslide site in Sitio Balakayo along the San Fernando–Talaingod–Kapalong–Tagum road.

Heavy equipment from DPWH Region 10 local district engineering offices, and the San Fernando municipal government are working on-site, though persistent bad weather continues to slow progress. /jpv

World.title: Groups decry criminal raps vs Nueva Vizcaya anti-mining advocates
World.content:
INQUIRER FILE PHOTO

MANILA, Philippines — Human rights and legal groups condemned what they called the “escalating, systematic harassment” of lawyers and community leaders opposing “destructive corporate mining” in Nueva Vizcaya.

The groups issued the statement after North Luzon Mineral Resources Corp. (NLMRC) filed a cyberlibel complaint this month against Fidel Santos and Edgardo Balgos, who represent local communities in Kasibu.

Last week, residents of Kasibu and Dupax del Norte went to the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources in Quezon City to demand the immediate revocation of NLMRC’s exploration permit.

Article continues after this 

The permit, issued on June 25, 2025, allowed the mining company to explore for gold, copper and other minerals across an estimated 4,456 hectares in Kasibu.

Kasibu is 39 kilometers from Dupax del Norte, where residents and police had intense confrontations over the operations of Woggle Corp.

READ: Fighting for their land, Vizcaya folk take aim vs mining

Last year, Woggle Corp. was granted a permit to explore for minerals across more than 3,100 hectares in the villages of Bitnong, Inaban, Mungia, Parai and Oyao. The MGB suspended the company’s exploration permit in an order dated Feb. 5.

READ: MGB temporarily stops mining firm’s activities in Nueva Vizcaya

Article continues after this 

Some community leaders and Bayombong Bishop Jose Elmer Mangalinao, who opposed Woggle Corp. and later NLMRC, also faced criminal complaints, although the case has since been dismissed.

Florentino Daynos, however, faces a cyberlibel complaint filed by NLMRC on June 19 over his support for a community barricade against mining exploration in Kasibu.

Article continues after this 

Two weeks earlier, Daynos and another community leader, Anthony Glenn Guingayan Sr., were informed that some residents had filed cyberlibel complaints against them.

Lian Buan, Southeast Asia researcher at Human Rights Watch (HRW), said: “Philippine prosecutors should dismiss criminal complaints filed by companies to silence communities raising concerns about their business operations.”

READ: Nueva Vizcaya residents want mining firm’s permit revoked

HRW said the pattern of criminal libel cases against community leaders and their legal representatives had the effect of strategic lawsuits against public participation, or SLAPP suits.

Santos said, “This [criminal libel case] creates a chilling effect, because if their defender is being harassed, then the more afraid they [residents] are.”

The National Union of People’s Lawyers (NUPL) described the criminal complaints as a “textbook” abuse of legal mechanisms intended not to vindicate a genuine legal right but to exhaust, intimidate and silence human rights defenders, activists and dissenters.

“It perverts the legal system and co-opts community institutions into instruments of political reprisal. Persona non grata resolutions, meanwhile, are hostile declarations that are never mere expressions of disagreement, but rather dangerous instruments of state and corporate sanction designed to stigmatize, isolate, and endanger advocates on the ground,” the NUPL said.

The Integrated Bar of the Philippines-Nueva Vizcaya Chapter said, “The filing of legal actions should never be used to discourage or chill legitimate advocacy.”

“Any attempt to intimidate members of the Bar from performing their professional responsibilities raises serious concerns for the administration of justice and the rule of law,” it said.

The NUPL said Santos merely sought transparency regarding the mining company’s legal compliance and the irreversible human and environmental toll of its operations in Kasibu.

“For fulfilling this professional and ethical duty, he is made to face malicious prosecution and public exclusion,” it said.

World.title: Police deploy 5,000 personnel for Sona in Western Visayas
World.content:
Western Visayas Map. INQUIRER FILES

ILOILO CITY — The Police Regional Office 6 (PRO6) has announced its complete readiness for the upcoming State of the Nation Address (Sona) 2026, deploying nearly 5,000 personnel and force multipliers across Western Visayas to guarantee a safe, peaceful, and orderly environment on Monday, July 27.

A total of 4,826 security personnel will be mobilized for the annual address of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.

The contingent comprises 3,905 officers from the Philippine National Police (PNP), 117 augmentation personnel from partner agencies—including the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), and Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP)—and 804 force multipliers composed of community volunteers and advocacy groups.

Article continues after this 

READ: Marcos on his forthcoming Sona: ‘Stay tuned for the next chapter’

Deployed units will carry out targeted security operations, including heightened police visibility, foot and mobile patrols, traffic management, medical response coordination, checkpoint and border controls, and civil disturbance management.

Additionally, Quick Reaction Teams (QRT) and the Reactionary Standby Support Force (RSSF) are placed on high alert for immediate dispatch in case of contingency.

Special security coverage will be designated at Freedom Parks, public assembly sites, and other venues expected to hold gatherings or events related to the Sona.

Police Brig. Gen. Randulf T. Tuaño, PRO6 Acting Director, emphasized that security operations are centered on maintaining peace, protecting the public, and upholding human rights.

Article continues after this 

“PRO6 is fully prepared to ensure a safe and peaceful Sona 2026. We have directed all our personnel to remain vigilant, disciplined, professional, and ready to respond to any eventuality. Public safety and security are our top priorities,” Tuaño said.

Tuaño also appealed to the public for full cooperation with local authorities, urging residents to adhere to security measures, maintain vigilance, and immediately report any suspicious activities to the nearest police station or through the Unified Emergency Hotline 911. INQ /mr

World.title: Planned river dredging necessary, says La Union town
World.content:
INQUIRER FILES

BAUANG, La Union – Faced with opposition against a plan to “dredge” Balili River that traverses this town, Bauang officials said this initiative will solve flooding.

The river is heavily silted and quickly overflows during rainy season, causing flooding in the town, according to Municipal Administrator Ronald Lee.

READ: Zambales dredging blamed for uprooted trees, coastal erosion

Article continues after this 

He said the Sanguniang Bayan (municipal council) has issued a “no objection resolution” for the project, but a desilting – not dredging – program and river reinforcement would be undertaken by different agencies and the provincial government.

Environmental group Koalisyon Isalbar ti Pintas ti La Union (KIPLU), Inc. expressed “deep dismay” at the council’s “no objection” resolution” for dredging the Balili River channel and delta.

The group said the resolution, “as currently worded, demonstrates a lack of discernment, inadequate safeguards, and a troubling disregard for genuine public consultation.”

“It authorizes dredging without requiring a comparative assessment of nature‑based solutions such as riparian restoration, reforestation, constructed wetlands, mangrove rehabilitation, and upstream sediment control measures that can reduce flood risk while restoring ecosystem services, ” KIPLU says.

Balili River, also known as the Naguilian River, has its headwater in Baguio City. The river discharges down the Benguet municipalities of La Trinidad and Sablan before entering La Union and draining into the West Philippine Sea through Bauang. It has a total length of 62.7 km (39.0 mi).

Article continues after this 

Lee said Bauang had decided to pursue the project, “but it is a multi-agency project.”

“I used to be against the project too, but there are scientific studies showing that the river is heavily silted and needed to be desilted so water can flow freely to the sea, ” he said.

Article continues after this 

Lee said, “Balili river used to br so deep we can dive into the water from the bridge. Now the water in most areas of the river is only waist-deep, and there are almost no more fish there, only shellfish.”

In a statement, KIPLU, said the project has “vague environmental safeguards.”

“The phrase ‘stringent measures’ (to safeguard the river) is insufficient without specific Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) requirements, turbidity and biodiversity monitoring, seasonal work windows, and a clear plan for safe disposal or beneficial reuse of dredged material,” it said.

Lee said the materials taken from the river will be used to reclaim the barangay Pilar which is continuously shrinking because of coastal erosion.

The environmental group still wants immediate suspension of any dredging permits or contracts until a transparent, independent comparative assessment (cost‑benefit and multi‑criteria) of dredging versus nature‑based solutions is completed and publicly released.

World.title: Negros town forms task force for local crab industry amid US export ban
World.content:
EB Magalona blue crabs. Ronnie Baldonado file photo

BACOLOD CITY—Mayor Matthew Louis Malacon of E.B. Magalona town, Negros Occidental created the Municipal Crab Industry Task Force (MCITF) to address the economic crisis that has hit the town’s blue swimming crab industry.

Known as the “Blue Crab Capital” of Negros Occidental, E.B. Magalona relies heavily on the blue swimming crab industry to sustain the livelihoods of fisherfolk, crab pickers, traders, and processors across its nine coastal barangays, the mayor said.

The local industry suffered a major setback following a recent export ban imposed by the United States National Marine Fisheries Service under the Marine Mammal Protection Act.

Article continues after this 

READ: Heavy rains due to Kiyapo trigger river swelling in Masbate town

The restriction effectively cut off local producers from their primary international market, leading to severe market disruptions and plunging local demand, declining prices for crab products, and income loss for local crab pickers, fisherfolk, traders, and processors, the mayor said

This has caused a drop in the price of the blue swimming crab in the domestic market, from P350 to P400 a kilo, to a low of P150 per kilo, Vice Mayor Marvin Malacon said.

The task force will find ways to address the plunge in prices and aid industry stakeholders, the vice mayor said.

The multi-sectoral body led by the mayor will initiate measures to cushion the impact and chart a path toward recovery.

Article continues after this 

The mayor said the task force is mandated to assess economic damages, maintain an updated registry of affected workers, coordinate technical and financial assistance with national government agencies, and explore market diversification and value-adding activities for local crab products.

In a bid to provide immediate financial relief, Mayor Malacon urged the Sangguniang Bayan of E.B. Magalona to urgently enact an ordinance granting a temporary tax holiday or local tax relief for eligible crab pickers, local fisherfolks, and directly affected businesses operating within the local crab supply chain.

Article continues after this 

Municipal departments—including Agriculture, Tourism, and Social Welfare—have been directed to roll out capability-building, skills training, and livelihood assistance programs to strengthen the resilience and long-term competitiveness of the local industry. INQ /mr

World.title: Election Campaigning Begins Ahead of Kazakhstan’s Kurultai Vote
World.content:
10945

ALMATY – Election campaigning officially began in Kazakhstan at 6:01 p.m. on July 23 ahead of the Aug. 23 elections to the Kurultai, with seven political parties competing for 145 seats in the representative body.

The campaign will run until midnight on Aug. 21, while Aug. 22 has been designated as the official day of silence before voting, the Central Election Commission’s press service reported.

The launch of the campaign follows the commission’s completion of party list registration, which registered 545 candidates nominated by the seven eligible political parties. Women, youth and persons with disabilities account for 43.9% of all candidates, exceeding the legal quota. The candidate list includes 172 women, 19 persons with disabilities, and 74 candidates under the age of 35, with an average candidate age of 45.4 years.

CEC accredits more international observers

Speaking at the CEC’s latest meeting on July 23, Deputy CEC Chairman Mukhtar Yerman said the commission has accredited 86 international observers representing 12 countries and five international organizations. The accreditation process, conducted in cooperation with the Foreign Ministry, will continue until Aug. 17.

The latest nominations include observers from Moldova, Albania, Armenia, Kuwait, Palestine and the International Parliamentarians Congress.

The CEC meeting brought together representatives of political parties, government agencies, the media and international observers, while regional election commissions and local authorities participated via videoconference.

More than 8,000 campaign sites prepared

According to local executive bodies, more than 8,000 locations have been prepared nationwide for campaign materials, while nearly 4,500 venues have been designated for meetings with voters.

CEC Chairman Nurlan Abdirov urged regional authorities to prepare additional reserve locations, particularly in major cities and densely populated regions, to ensure equal campaigning opportunities for all parties.

“Given the high level of competition and activity demonstrated during the nomination and registration stages of this campaign, local authorities should not limit themselves to the existing number of campaign sites and meeting venues but also provide a reasonable reserve,” he said.

CEC member Lyazzat Suyindik reminded political parties of several amendments to election legislation introduced for the current campaign. Among the new provisions is a ban on photographing or filming completed ballots and sharing such images on election day, a measure intended to protect the secrecy of the vote and ensure voters can make independent choices. The updated legislation also prohibits the use of campaign materials produced for previous election campaigns.

The elections for Kazakhstan’s Kurultai are scheduled for Aug. 23.
